name: Flood Plain Management Study — Clam River, Wexford County, Michigan.pdf
description: Historic Soil Conservation Service study of the Clam River, Lake Cadillac, Lake Mitchell and Pleasant Lake. It includes flood-hazard photomaps, profiles and 10-, 50-, 100- and 500-year discharge/elevation tables. It is receptor and watershed context, not proof of PFAS contamination or source attribution.

name: EPA Region 5 Michigan First-Quarter 2010 QNCR.pdf
description: EPA Region 5 Quarterly Non-Compliance Report dated March 15, 2010 for the October–December 2009 quarter. Its Cadillac WWTP entry lists total mercury at outfall 001A, violation date July 31, 2005, with status 'NC — continuing noncompliance.'

name: EPA ICIS Michigan Second-Quarter 2014 QNCR.pdf
description: EPA ICIS Quarterly Non-Compliance Report for January–March 2014. The Cadillac WWTP detail row records an overdue DMR for outfall 001, violation date December 31, 2013, status date February 20, 2014, and code 2D reporting violation; no linked enforcement action or final order is shown.

name: N3862 Scheduled Inspection — Wexford County Landfill.pdf
description: November 6, 2017 AQD scheduled inspection for state registration N3862. The report records compliance, a 3.45-million-Mg design capacity, active landfill-gas collection and flare, post-closure groundwater-remediation aeration ponds and an exempt leachate evaporation system. The separate '(1)' filename was an exact duplicate and is not carried forward.

name: Wexford County Landfill Tier 2 NMOC Results.pdf
description: March 10, 2021 report on January 19–21 Tier 2 sampling. LandGEM estimates 35.81 Mg/year average and 38.64 Mg/year maximum NMOC for 2021, below the 50-Mg/year threshold, while projecting later threshold crossings under its stated waste assumptions. Retesting was due by January 19, 2026.

name: N3862 Renewable Operating Permit Staff Report.pdf
description: August 15, 2022 staff report and September 15 addendum for MI-ROP-N3862-2022. It records leachate injection beginning in early 2019, closure/removal of the aeration ponds since 2017, 2021 emissions, March 2022 Tier 2 NMOC calculations and AQD's expected-compliance finding.

name: Cadillac WWTP CWSRF Project Plan and Funding Proposal.pdf
description: February 2, 2026 Council communication and F&V proposal for a $36,800 CWSRF project plan. Candidate improvements include headworks, blowers, UV disinfection, solids handling, biogas use and site repairs; the selected construction project was not yet fixed by this planning proposal.

name: September 8 2009 Special Meeting Minutes.pdf
description: Official special-meeting minutes record unanimous approval of a two-year agreement for Cadillac to accept and treat Wexford County Landfill leachate, effective July 1, 2009 through June 30, 2011. The minutes also address separate municipal well-field planning; that material is not treated as PFAS evidence.

name: 2022-09-13-Draft-Exec-Packet.pdf
description: The packet preserves EGLE's August 18, 2022 fiscal-year 2021 evaluation of Wexford County Landfill. EGLE calculated a $131,920.40 perpetual-care shortfall and flagged possible unauthorized waste imports for written response; the letter is an evaluation and response request, not a final adjudication.

name: Council Packet 7-20-26.pdf
description: The packet schedules a PFAS municipal-water project-plan action and describes an $8.206 million Emerging Contaminants Grant designation for extending water service to private-well users in response areas. The included resolution is unsigned and blank, so the packet does not prove adoption, receipt of funds or construction.

name: Cadillac_1988_Feasibility_Study_FontFixed_OCR.pdf
description: April 1988 MDNR/E.C. Jordan interim feasibility study identifies five known or probable industrial-park source areas and seven groundwater plumes involving VOCs and hexavalent chromium, and discusses treated-groundwater discharge options. It predates the PFAS investigation and is not evidence of PFAS source attribution.

name: Hydrogeologic_Investigation_-_1140_Plett_Rd_Cadillac_MI.md.pdf
description: August 7, 2026 public-records and hydrogeologic working report for 1140 Plett Road. It separates confirmed, probable, possible and unknown findings and identifies unresolved parcel-well, drainage, elevation and groundwater-flow questions. It is retained as a research synthesis and records-request plan, not a primary agency finding.

name: City of Cadillac FY2019 CAFR.pdf
description: The audited report for the fiscal year ended June 30, 2019 states that revenue from treatment of Wexford County Landfill leachate exceeded budget by $44,691. It corroborates treatment activity but does not state total gallons, PFAS content or treatment performance.

name: December 3 2018 City Council Packet [Item 1086].pdf
description: The packet preserves the City's first council-level report of PFAS municipal-water sampling results and states that the reported samples were non-detect. It is a dated public record, not a claim about later sampling.

name: December 17 2018 City Council Packet [Item 1088].pdf
description: The packet gives a follow-up municipal-water PFAS update and states that all tested wellfield sites were non-detect at that time.

name: November 20 2017 City Council Packet [Item 992].pdf
description: The packet includes a proposed resolution opposing the Wexford County Landfill leachate-injection well and describes Cadillac's long-running treatment of landfill leachate under its pretreatment and discharge programs.

name: December 4 2017 City Council Packet [Item 994].pdf
description: The packet preserves the subsequent council record concerning the opposition resolution and Cadillac's treatment of Wexford County Landfill leachate.

name: April 1 2019 City Council Packet [Item 1123].pdf
description: The packet's budget material states that leachate-treatment revenue was expected to end after the landfill's deep-injection well became operational. The statement documents an expectation at that date, not independent proof of cessation.

name: June 17 2024 City Council Packet [Item 2591].pdf
description: The packet preserves the public-record appeal and hearing material concerning PFAS and LDFA cleanup-discharge records, including the parties' testimony and source-document dispute.

name: September 16 2024 City Council Packet [Item 2604].pdf
description: The packet records council discussion of PFAS in the LDFA groundwater-cleanup discharge to the Clam River, including cited concentration and regulatory-threshold context.

name: October 7 2024 City Council Packet [Item 2611].pdf
description: The packet records private-well PFAS concerns, a cited result and the City's request for clearer agency communication. The cited value is preserved as a statement in the packet, not independently reinterpreted.

name: October 21 2024 City Council Packet [Item 2614].pdf
description: The packet records an LDFA commitment to test as many as five cleanup wells for PFAS, establishing a dated monitoring decision without implying results were already available.

name: November 18 2024 City Council Packet [Item 2637].pdf
description: The packet preserves continuing public and LDFA discussion of PFAS and the industrial-park groundwater-cleanup system.

name: December 2 2024 City Council Packet [Item 2640].pdf
description: The packet includes a detailed city-attorney and LDFA briefing on industrial sources, the historic cleanup system and PFAS testing. Its source-attribution statements remain attributed to the speakers and documents presented.

name: January 21 2025 City Council Packet [Item 2656].pdf
description: The packet attaches the MPART Cadillac Area of Interest FAQ and preserves the City's public discussion of the investigation and response.

name: February 18 2025 City Council Packet [Item 2706].pdf
description: The packet records discussion of contaminated areas, the private-water connection challenge, legal options and the City's operational PFAS response.

name: April 7 2025 City Council Packet [Item 2737].pdf
description: The packet describes the City's goal of connecting approximately 224 parcels to municipal water and outlines testing and response planning. The goal is not presented as completed construction.

name: April 21 2025 City Council Packet [Item 2745].pdf
description: The packet contains a biosolids PFAS update stating that the recent PFOS/PFAS testing discussed by the City was non-detect.

name: May 19 2025 City Council Packet [Item 2768].pdf
description: The packet records the City's municipal-well non-detect statement and updates wastewater and private-well testing activity.

name: June 2 2025 City Council Packet [Item 2772].pdf
description: The packet preserves private-well testing, biosolids and public-resource-fair updates together with council and community discussion.

name: July 21 2025 City Council Packet [Item 2787].pdf
description: The packet reports progress on 48 private-well tests and preserves related Clam River concerns and response discussion.

name: August 4 2025 City Council Packet [Item 2791].pdf
description: The packet updates the number of affected homes, municipal-water availability and the bottled-water program. Counts are preserved as the City's dated report.

name: August 18 2025 City Council Packet [Item 2796].pdf
description: The packet preserves the City's state-appropriations testimony and funding update for the PFAS water-response project.

name: September 2 2025 City Council Packet [Item 2806].pdf
description: The packet records the City's statement that the final private-well results were non-detect and that infrastructure funding efforts would continue.

name: October 20 2025 City Council Packet [Item 2829].pdf
description: The packet records that an anticipated $8 million state appropriation was not included and documents the City's continued funding effort.

name: December 1 2025 City Council Packet [Item 2849].pdf
description: The packet preserves discussion of laboratory comparability and WWTP effluent PFAS results. It retains the reported findings without merging unlike analytical records.

name: December 15 2025 City Council Packet [Item 2854].pdf
description: The packet contains PFAS grant talking points and records a major municipal-water-connection grant development.

name: January 20 2026 City Council Packet [Item 2867].pdf
description: The packet records state sampling updates, the announced $8.2 million emerging-contaminants grant and the City's management-plan work.

name: February 2 2026 City Council Packet [Item 2874].pdf
description: The packet records an additional $1.46 million federal funding development for the PFAS municipal-water project.

name: March 2 2026 City Council Packet [Item 2884].pdf
description: The packet records an LDFA carbon-filter vessel replacement intended for PFAS capture in the cleanup system, adding operational evidence beyond the recurring status summary.

name: April 6 2026 City Council Packet [Item 2902].pdf
description: The packet records that higher-PFAS cleanup flows were rerouted through the carbon system, preserving a dated operational response statement.

name: May 18 2026 City Council Packet [Item 2925].pdf
description: The packet contains a biosolids PFAS testing update reporting results below the thresholds discussed by the City. The statement is preserved with its original regulatory context.

name: June 15 2026 City Council Packet [Item 2939].pdf
description: The packet preserves budget and pre-project engineering material for the emerging-contaminants water grant.

name: Most Recent Item August 17 2026 City Council Packet [Item 2960].pdf
description: The packet updates the $8.2 million and federal-grant work and includes the PFAS Water System Improvements planning record available to council in August 2026.

name: May 21 2018 City Council Packet [Item 1047].pdf
description: The packet's FY2018 budget amendment increases the leachate-revenue line from $150,000 to $400,000 and identifies the reason as additional treatment of Wexford County Landfill leachate. It documents budgeted revenue, not PFAS concentration or treatment performance.

name: June 3 2019 City Council Packet [Item 1142].pdf
description: The packet's budget amendment increases the leachate-revenue line from $150,000 to $450,000 and attributes the change to additional leachate-treatment revenue. This qualifies the earlier expectation that landfill-related revenue would end.

name: March 3 2025 City Council Packet [Item 2715].pdf
description: The packet preserves the citizens-advisory PFAS survey, the City's February response update and notice of the February 26 MPART sessions. Survey responses and public statements remain attributed to their sources.

name: March 17 2025 City Council Packet [Item 2731].pdf
description: The packet records publication of the MPART session video and heat-map materials and an update to the United Way 211 referral system for PFAS assistance.

name: June 16 2025 City Council Packet [Item 2777].pdf
description: The packet records council approval associated with the June 27 PFAS Resource Fair and preserves related LDFA and community-response discussion.

name: September 15 2025 City Council Packet [Item 2809].pdf
description: The packet records that the donated bottled-water supply had been exhausted and that the delivery program ended, together with notice sent to participating residents and continued funding advocacy.

name: September 26 2025 City Council Special Meeting Packet [Item 2814].pdf
description: The packet describes the planned three-laboratory PFAS comparability study using simultaneous samples from approximately 20 residences. It records the study design before the later findings.

name: May 19 2025 City Council Meeting Minutes.pdf
description: Official minutes preserve the May 19 PFAS update, including private-well test counts and retesting after possible sample contamination, attributed biosolids and municipal-water statements, planned mapping and infrastructure work, and the stated 2019 loss of landfill-leachate treatment revenue.
